title: No barber shaves exactly those who do not shave themselves
statement: For any binary relation `shaves` on any domain, there is no element b such that for every x, b shaves x if and only if x does not shave x.

formal.statement: (assert (not (exists ((b Person)) (forall ((x Person)) (= (shaves b x) (not (shaves x x)))))))

provenance.source: authored from the S:logic-and-proof strand of the math-education concept graph; statement written here, not copied

notes: OPEN IN THIS LEDGER, NOT IN MATHEMATICS. axeyum gets the right VERDICT and no usable evidence, which is a more interesting failure than returning `unknown`. Measured 2026-08-14 with `cargo run -q -p axeyum-bench --example smtcomp_cli -- --evidence artifacts/facts/smt2/neg-barber-no-such-barber.smt2`: it printed `; evidence kind=unsat-drat certified=0 recheck=na arena=FAIL ms=171` and then `unsat`. Read that line carefully, because two of its fields are misreported by the harness rather than by the solver. The evidence object is a BARE `Evidence::Unsat(None)` -- no certificate at all -- but `Evidence::kind_label` maps every `Unsat` variant to the string `unsat-drat`, so the line names a DRAT proof that does not exist; and `Evidence::check` returns `Ok(false)` for a bare unsat, which the CLI renders as `arena=FAIL`, i.e. as though a certificate had been examined and found wanting. `Evidence::check_outcome` on the same input correctly answers `NothingToCheck(UncertifiedUnsat)`. The verdict is right, the certificate is absent, and the status here stays `open` because an uncertified unsat is not evidence under this schema. The proposition is one universal instantiation (x := b) away from the already-proved F:no-self-negating-proposition -- but that instantiation step is one no component of ours performed or recorded.
